To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a Matlab®-based toolkit that can be applied to a broad class of discretisation and solution techniques, which is open-source and can be used for reproducible research and comparison of different methods.
• We developed an open-source MATLAB® implementation that can be used for the development, testing and comparison of numerical methods for reservoir simulation.

(i) a flexible grid representation for complex grids is required for efficient numerical methods; (ii) the toolkit is a flexible platform for testing and comparing discretisation and solution algorithms for complex grids; (iii) the toolkit is an efficient test platform that can be used to test, verify, validate and compare (new) numerical methods for complex grids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the implementation of numerical methods on complex grids and the development and testing of advanced methods for efficient reservoir simulation.
developing a toolkit that can be easily used to implement and test new discretisation methods and solution methods on complex grids.
the development of efficient, accurate and reliable numerical methods and tools for the modelling of flow in complex geological reservoirs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the toolkit is a valuable tool for the development and verification of new discretisation methods and solvers for reservoir simulation.

the toolkit has been developed to support the development and validation of new numerical methods on complex unstructured grids, and to provide a common platform for testing and comparing new methods with existing ones.
the toolkit is an open-source Matlab implementation of consistent discretisation on complex grids.

we provide a toolkit that can be considered as a testbed for new discretisation and numerical methods in reservoir simulation, with the aim of supporting reproducible research in the community.
this paper provides a toolkit that can be applied for testing and validating new numerical methods for subsur-face flow simulations, and that can be used in research and education.

the toolkit can be used as a test platform for new discretisation and solvers and as a platform for reproducible research.
